subject: Quadrant Health — commercial alignment & migration playbook
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@quadranthealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quadrant Health — initial offer + migration guardrails

Hi Maria,

Thanks for the time earlier. Per our conversation I pulled together an offer that targets the two constraints you called out: matching the incumbent unit economics for inference while reducing integration risk and go-live time. Attached is a concise workbook (Quadrant_RFP_Q3.xlsx) and the proposal summary (Redwood_Replacement_Offer_v1.pdf).

High level proposal: 
- Price match on core text-generation token unit for year 1 (applies to hosted + dedicated fallback).
- Phased onboarding credits: $60k total, applied across pilot + production ramp.
- 4-week technical onboarding window (priority queue) with a guaranteed go-live readiness checkpoint and SLOs for inference latency during pilot.

We can also include an 8-week rollback window tied to traffic migration so your ops team has a deterministic escape path if anything unexpected happens.

Next steps: if the economics look reasonable, can we schedule a 30-min session Thursday to align procurement language and SLAs? I copied Jordan from contracts so he can start drafting the commercial terms you’ll need.

Thanks — look forward to moving this quickly.

— Logan
Logan Wright | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147

Attachment: Quadrant_RFP_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: Redwood_Replacement_Offer_v1.pdf (proposal summary)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@quadranthealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quadranthealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quadrant Health — initial offer + migration guardrails

Logan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. I forwarded to procurement and engineering; a few reactions from ops/finance after a fast read: 

- The price-match helps, but year-1 match alone isn't sufficient — we need a predictable unit price for at least 18 months to budget for FY27.
- The onboarding credit looks sensible; want to understand how that would be applied (invoice credit vs. service credit).
- Need explicit language on data handling and audit trails (SOC2 + access logs) — we provide PHI-adjacent workloads and must ensure comms with legal.

Can you also provide a technical runbook excerpt for the pilot (how Redwood handles KV cache, batching, and fallthrough to dedicated capacity)? Our infra lead asked for those details before we commit to the pilot window.

Availability: Thurs 30th between 11–12 PT or Friday morning.

— Maria
Maria Lopez | Sr. Procurement Manager | Quadrant Health
maria.lopez@quadranthealth.com

Attachment: Quadrant_Internal_Notes.txt (internal comments)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@quadranthealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quadrant Health — initial offer + migration guardrails

Maria — great questions, appreciate the clarity. Short answers and proposed commercial edits below; Grace from Solutions is on thread and will follow up with the runbook excerpt.

Pricing term: we can extend the price-match to 18 months for the same committed usage band; after 18 months we’d revert to published list pricing with a 60-day notice and a cap on delta for the first 90 days.

Credit application: credits are applied as invoice-level dollar credits (applied monthly during ramp) — this is standard for reserved onboarding credits. If procurement prefers a service credit structure, we can model it but I’ve found invoice credits are simplest for treasury.

Data & compliance: Redwood provides SOC2 Type II, monthly audit-log exports, and can put a customer-specific KMS policy in place for Private deployments. Jordan — can your legal team draft a clause referencing audit-log retention and KMS controls?

Pilot runbook ask: Grace, can you drop a 1–2 page excerpt and the pilot success metrics into Drive and I’ll share? Maria, want to confirm Thurs 30 at 11 PT for a 30-minute commercial+tech sync.

Thanks — Logan

Attachment: Pricing_Summary_Table.xlsx (pricing bands)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@quadranthealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quadrant Health — initial offer + migration guardrails

Hi Maria — quick technical excerpt below; I'll also upload a 2-page pilot runbook to the Drive link Logan shared.

Pilot runbook excerpt:
- Scope: pilot covers 3 inference endpoints (chat, embeddings, rerank). Traffic cap: up to 2M tokens/day during pilot.
- Caching & batching: Redwood will configure persistent prefix caching for steady-state prompts and a KV cache policy tuned to your average seq length (we recommend 1–2k context for retrieval flows). We’ll enable adaptive batching with a 40ms max latency tail target for interactive endpoints.
- Fallthrough behavior: if hosted capacity hits internal thresholds we route to Dedicated pool dedicated to Quadrant (same model family, quantization profile). Requests logged with trace IDs; we expose a /trace API for post-mortem.
- Success metrics (pilot): 95th percentile latency < 250ms for chat 1k tokens; embedding throughput >= 600/s; zero PII leaks in 1000 sampled responses (evaluated by your compliance team).

Onboarding timeline: Week 0: kickoff & infra validation; Week 1–2: pilot configuration + smoke tests; Week 3: pilot run; Week 4: production ramp & SLA handover.

If you want additional contractual guarantees around latency or a financial SLA, we can propose a limited SLA credit schedule tied to 95/99 latency bands.

— Grace
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

Attachment: Pilot_Runbook_QH_exerpt.docx (docx)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@quadranthealth.com>

Cc: procurement@quadranthealth.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quadrant Health — initial offer + migration guardrails

Logan / Grace / Jordan — thanks, that helps a lot. Procurement reviewed the invoice-credit approach and is fine with that model. We also appreciate the 18-month price-match commitment. A couple final asks before we route to legal: 

1) Can Jordan draft the KMS + audit-log clause and a simple SLA credit schedule (sample language) we can attach to the Statement of Work?
2) Confirm the onboarding credit will not trigger any revenue recognition clawbacks on our side (i.e., show as a vendor credit line item on invoices).
3) We want to lock the pilot traffic cap and the rollback window in the SOW.

If you can get a redlineable SOW and the two clause drafts by EOD Monday, procurement will tee this up for a Tuesday signature meeting with our CFO.

If that timeline works, we are ready to move forward.

— Maria

Attachment: Quadrant_Purchase_Request.pdf (pdf)
